segmentation.text: A pedestrian
walking or otherwise traveling on a sidewalk
who encounters an obstruction to his or her mobility on the sidewalk,
including, without limitation, a short section of the sidewalk that is missing or impassable,
may proceed
with due care
on the immediately adjacent highway to move around such an obstruction.
Such a pedestrian:
(a) Must walk or otherwise travel as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk
as possible;
(b) May walk or otherwise travel on the highway in the direction he or she was walking or traveling on the sidewalk, regardless of the direction of traffic;
(c) May walk or otherwise travel in a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable;
and (d) Must return to the sidewalk
as soon as practicable.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed whole.

'walking or otherwise traveling' is the pedestrian moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'on a sidewalk' is its footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a sidewalk (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; not a crosswalk), the sidewalk it later leaves.

'an obstruction to his or her mobility' is st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user'); 'encounters' is the pedestrian's body coming within the encounter reach of it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') while on the sidewalk; 'on the sidewalk' is read through the pedestrian being on that sidewalk when it meets the object, no atom relating the object's region to the sidewalk's.

A missing or impassable section of sidewalk is no object: st.obstruction is 'a physical object', and st.sidewalk says nothing of whether a stretch of it can be traversed. The examples extend the trigger to a stretch of sidewalk that cannot be walked, which no atom carries: the gap on this span. The nearest atoms are named only to show the shortfall.
'may proceed' is the pedestrian moving on (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) after the encounter; the permission is the occasion of the duties (a) and (d).

'on the immediately adjacent highway' is the pedestrian off every sidewalk (rel.occupies of no st.sidewalk) and on a travel region (st.travel_region, read through the quantifier: a lane, roadway, shoulder or bicycle lane) that lies on (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') the same highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way ... including sidewalks and shoulders'; not the roadway) as the sidewalk it left; 'to move around such an obstruction' is that departure following the encounter with the same obstruction, the pedestrian having stayed off the sidewalk since.
'Such a pedestrian' is the subject: DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, as selected by the trigger spans.

'as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk' is the ground distance from the pedestrian's body to the sidewalk it left (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'; not occupancy), which the standard bounds.

'a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path ('lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'), the pedestrian occupying it (rel.occupies); the words name the lane's kind, not road users, so no aggregate is read. 'if the area between the lane and the sidewalk is impassable' needs the impassable stretch of ground between them, which no atom carries: the gap on this span; st.sidewalk is the nearest.

operationalizations.convention: pedestrian shy distance: the pedestrian keeps as near the sidewalk as it can where its body lies within the shy distance of the sidewalk it left, or, where the obstruction itself reaches off the sidewalk, within the shy distance of that obstruction (st.region_geometry ground distances)

residues.why: 'with due care' qualifies the permission to proceed; duties (a) and (d) bind a pedestrian who has gone onto the highway around the obstruction whether or not it did so with due care

the permission to travel in the direction of the sidewalk travel, whatever the direction of traffic, relaxes rules on the side a pedestrian walks; duty (a) is the same whichever way the pedestrian walks

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. There are a st.sidewalk S and a st.obstruction O (or, through the gap, an impassable section of S) such that at an earlier observation the subject, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and occupying S (rel.occupies), had its body within p.obstruction_encounter_reach of O (st.region_geometry), and at every observation since (the past mirror of until) the subject has occupied no st.sidewalk and has occupied a st.travel_region lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway S lies on.
obligation: For every such S and O (re-bound with their whole selection): the ground distance from the subject's body to S (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pedestrian_side_margin, or the ground distance from its body to O is at most p.pedestrian_side_margin. Excepted where the subject occupies a st.bicycle_lane_or_path and the area between that lane and S is impassable (gap: no atom carries an impassable stretch).

narrowings.why: 'as far ... as possible' is read as within a shy distance of the sidewalk, or of the obstruction where it reaches off the sidewalk; other limits on what is possible are not read

segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Be prepared to stop.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'), claimed as ru.aggregate; its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct the words require of it (lights in use, motion) is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service ... kind ∈ {..., regulatory_agency, ...}'), not read as an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points'; no clearance or order of arrival is read from it). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'or preparing to move', as the section defines it (s8): the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible, 'an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body'; not a distance, not a lit lamp) showing an arm signal (sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator left or right: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction: no heading of the vehicle is read. The vehicle is quantified in the formula, never a binder.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}, facing ∈ {front, rear, side}'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix which lights meet the requirements: a lamp lit on the approached vehicle of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read, the words name lights only.

'any other vehicle' is the defined term vehicle, admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); its exclusions (devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices, electric scooters) are the reading's classification under that id, never expanded here. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle: the subject and it are not the same road user. 'the driver' is a relational role, not an aggregate: read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction: 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer, the other roles are not law enforcement officers. The exception holds where such a device governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a position) a travel region (st.travel_region, read only through the quantifier, as the abstract kind requires) the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'otherwise directed' admits any indication the officer gives there.

The section's own definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' is the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible) showing an indication; '(a) A movement of the vehicle' is its kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle' is sig.hand_signal ('a driver's or rider's arm signal') with a meaning other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits further indications, of which a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator, 'the signal that precedes a manoeuvre') is the one the vocabulary carries. 'about to move' is an imminent movement read through these indications.

operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the subject is prepared to stop where the distance it needs to come to 'complete cessation from movement' (the stop when required, DEF-NRS-484A-255) — its speed times the perception-reaction time plus its speed squared over twice the braking deceleration — does not exceed the gap between its body and the approached vehicle's (rel.surface_gap); the deceleration is selected by the surface: ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject to e, and e's sig.hand_signal meaning other than no_signal or its sig.turn_indicator other than off); and e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing from the subject, longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach of centre distance (rel.centre_distance). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
obligation: Surrogate. For every road user e selected as in the applicability (re-bound with its whole selection: class, lamp, moving or preparing, ahead within the reach), the subject's stopping distance at the observation — kin.speed × p.driver_reaction_time plus kin.speed squared divided by twice the deceleration, the deceleration being p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_decel_dry — is at most the gap between the subject's body and e's (rel.surface_gap).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

'preparing to move', which the section defines as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is an imminent movement, read through the visible indications the definition lists (movement, hand signals) and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible), not as what the driver perceived
'prepared to stop' is read only as the ability to stop short of the approached vehicle at the current speed; readiness of mind is not observed and the rule is a surrogate

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The subject vehicle moves toward an ambulance (authorized emergency vehicle) ahead of it within the approach reach; the ambulance moves with a red front warning lamp flashing. The subject's speed gives a stopping distance (reaction plus braking) longer than the surface gap to the ambulance.

scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject has slowed so that its stopping distance is shorter than the surface gap to the ambulance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives at speed; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone and does not arise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe warning lamps, so whether the ambulance uses its flashing lights is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a police officer directing traffic (dev.human_direction, role police_officer) governs the lane the subject occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Icy road (env.ice_or_snow). The subject's speed and gap would allow a stop on a dry surface but not at the ice deceleration; the ambulance ahead is stopped and its driver gives an arm signal, visible from the subject (preparing to move), with its red front lamp flashing.

segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
If possible,
drive in a lane that is not adjacent to the lane in which the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency is moving,
unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, not an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach (rel.centre_distance; no clearance read). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move', as defined in s10: visible from the subject (rel.visible) with an arm signal (sig.hand_signal other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix the lights: a lamp lit of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); exclusions are the reading's. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle. 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer; excepted where such a device governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'drive in a lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies; st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'), the lane being the subject's own feature; 'the lane in which the ... vehicle ... is moving' is a lane the approached vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane). 'adjacent' is read in two ways the contracts carry: the left or right neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; not the marking between the lanes), and, for a vehicle moving against the subject's direction, the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions — each of lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'), their designated directions opposed (st.lane_direction) — on one and the same roadway that both road users occupy (st.roadway, 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate', so a divided highway's opposing lanes are never adjacent). A lane is not adjacent to itself.

The section's definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: visible from the subject (rel.visible); '(a) A movement of the vehicle' kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator). 'about to move' is read through these indications.

operationalizations.convention: lane-change time: moving away from the vehicle's lane is possible once the approach has lasted the time a driver needs to perceive the vehicle and change one lane, and only where the subject's way carries a candidate lane: a lane on the same highway as the subject's lane (st.on_way) whose designated direction points the subject's way (st.lane_direction, positive dot product with the subject's lane direction) and that is not adjacent to the vehicle's lane

operationalizations.standard: unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance and lane availability: a candidate lane is impossible (roadway) where a temporary traffic control device governs it, and unsafe (traffic) where a road user occupying it, other than the subject (any road user using the highway: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances', DEF-NRS-484A-285, read without exclusion), is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface (ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry); weather makes the move unsafe where the road is icy or snow-covered, or the visibility (env.visibility) is shorter than the distance the subject travels at its speed in the lane-change time

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). obligation: For every e selected as in the applicability for which that whole selection has held at every observation of the window behind of length p.emergency_lane_change_window, every st.lane Le that e occupies and every st.lane Ls that the subject occupies: Ls is not adjacent to Le, or the move is excused. Excused where env.ice_or_snow holds; or env.visibility is below the subject's kin.speed × p.emergency_lane_change_window; or no candidate lane is open and clear. A candidate lane C is a st.lane lying on (st.on_way) the same st.highway as Ls, whose designated direction has a positive dot product with Ls's, and which is not adjacent to Le in the sense above; C is open and clear where no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs) and no road user u other than the subject occupying C has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

'lawfully' is the lawfulness of the rider's own conduct under every rule engaged for it, which no atom carries and no composition of a named rule states: the gap on this span. 'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride, having two tandem wheels ...'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each is the admitted aggregate, claimed whole, never expanded into classes; the protected road user is a member of any of the three.

proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:

move the vehicle to the lane to the immediate left,
if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe.

The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ...'), 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole; the overtaken road user is a member of any of them.

'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance') between the subject and it, with the overtaking heading tolerance.

'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the pass is made with due care where the subject's body never touches the overtaken rider's (rel.contact) and the rider is never made to brake harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative) while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); care is a state of mind, read only through this outcome

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter
at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter,
and shall not move again to the right side of the highway
until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.213 and 484B.217 [NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c, NRS-484B-217-2],

when passing to the left of a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, this paragraph authorizes the driver, if it is safe, to pass: (1) To the left of the center of the highway. (2) In a no-passing zone.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only, the side being read by b7. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.
'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies) being the stated one (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction'; not the marking between lanes). 'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

'pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter' (the overtaken road user of b2, its aggregates claimed again for these words): at every observation of the pass at which the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), the rider lies on the subject's right: the lateral component of its bearing in the subject's frame (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)') is negative.

operationalizations.standard: at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle
operationalizations.convention: lateral passing clearance: the distance between the nearest points of the two bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', which is the distance between any portion of the vehicle and the rider's device) is at least the larger of the stated 3 feet and the bicyclist operating-space clearance the reading sets, at every observation at which the two are side by side

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty to pass on the left at a safe distance unchanged

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of that window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); and at some observation of that window at which the two were side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r occupied a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is the literal one.
obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window at which the subject and r are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r lies on the subject's right (rel.bearing from the subject, lateral component negative) and the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) is at least the larger of the literal 3 ft and p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'a safe distance' is read as one lateral clearance the reading sets, never below the stated 3 feet; the clearance does not grow with the subject's speed

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Road with one lane in the subject's direction; a bicycle rides in it. The subject car overtakes the bicycle on its left with a body-to-body gap below 3 feet while side by side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass, the subject car keeping a gap above both 3 feet and the safe-gap clearance while side by side, the bicycle on its right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes another car on a one-lane road; no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the gap between bodies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes an electric scooter on the scooter's right, with a wide gap: while side by side the scooter lies on the subject's left.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The road has two lanes in the subject's direction; the subject passes a bicycle.

Here the pass is read while under way — the bodies side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance) after the rider was ahead within the window — and once completed, from the observation at which the concept rises, within the window.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.
'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies) being the stated one (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction'). 'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

'move again to the right side of the highway': having moved out to the left of the rider (rel.bearing from the subject, lateral component negative: the rider on its right), the subject turns back toward the side the rider keeps: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) for a lane L (st.lane) the rider occupies (rel.occupies) — 'a, moving, points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance'. The concept says nothing of whether the subject occupies L, so it reads a move back toward the rider's lane from the opposing lane or from the left part of the rider's lane alike. 'again' fixes the order: the subject first had the rider on its right.

operationalizations.standard: until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle
operationalizations.convention: time headway: the subject (the vehicle) is safely clear of the overtaken rider where the rider is behind it (rel.bearing longitudinal component negative, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with a gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap) of at least the rider's speed times the following headway for the surface — ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry — so that the rider, following, keeps the headway a following road user keeps

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty not to move back right before being clear unchanged

applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. Some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos), is being overtaken by the subject: at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window r was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with aligned headings, and either r is not yet behind the subject or drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) (window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos) has risen at some observation of that window; r lies on the subject's right (rel.bearing lateral component negative); and r occupies a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is the literal one.
obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), where r is not safely clear behind the subject — that is, not (r behind the subject, rel.bearing longitudinal component negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, with rel.surface_gap at least r's kin.speed × the headway: p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry) — the subject does not move to the right: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) with sin_tol p.course_departure_sin_tol and speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance holds for no st.lane L that r occupies (rel.occupies).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'move again to the right side of the highway' is read as the subject's heading turned to the right of the rider's lane direction beyond the course tolerance, after it has the rider on its right; a gradual drift within that tolerance is not read
'safely clear' is read as the rider behind the subject at a time-headway gap at the rider's speed; the rider's own braking ability is not otherwise read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Road with one lane in the subject's direction; the subject car moves out left and overtakes a bicycle; while the bicycle is still beside it, the subject car steers back to the right, its heading turning right of the lane's direction beyond the course tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass; the subject car keeps its course until the bicycle is behind it at a gap above the bicycle's speed times the dry headway, then steers back right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes another car on a one-lane road and steers back; no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe headings.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car completes the pass of an electric scooter and steers back right at once, the scooter behind it at a gap below its speed times the dry headway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The road has two lanes in the subject's direction; the subject passes a bicycle and steers back right while beside it.
